claims.text: Higher atomic size mismatch induces increased local lattice distortion in refractory high-entropy alloys.
Increased local lattice distortion enhances high-temperature mechanical strength.
Increased local lattice distortion enhances thermoelastic stability.
Local lattice distortion impedes dislocation mobility.
Local lattice distortion stabilizes the elastic response at high temperature.
The proposed comparison assumes single-phase refractory high-entropy alloys with uniform elemental distributions and equivalent processing histories.
Compositional tailoring can produce an alloy series with greater atomic size mismatch and a control series with minimized size mismatch.
High-temperature mechanical and thermoelastic testing should be conducted under sustained and cyclic thermal exposure while phase stability is maintained.
Diffraction peak broadening and local strain measurements can quantify local lattice distortion.
Enhanced lattice distortion creates local stress fields.
Distortion-associated local stress fields impede dislocation motion.
Enhanced lattice distortion influences phonon behavior.
Alloys with greater lattice distortion will retain higher yield strength than lower-distortion control alloys.
Alloys with greater lattice distortion will exhibit a more stable thermoelastic modulus than lower-distortion control alloys.
The proposed mechanism is limited to single-phase refractory high-entropy alloys without phase transformations or extraneous defect influences.
The magnitude of mechanical and thermoelastic improvement may depend on composition and processing conditions.
A lack of statistically significant improvement in strength retention and thermoelastic stability in the high-mismatch series would falsify the hypothesis.
A lack of correlation between measured lattice distortion and mechanical-performance differences would falsify the hypothesis.
